newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy says no hope of more Albanian ship survivors.
newsitem.headline: Italy says no hope of more Albanian ship survivors.

text.p: Italy said on Saturday there was no hope of finding any more survivors from an Albanian refugee boat that sank after a collision with a navy ship in the Adriatic, killing at least four people.

"There are no longer plausible possibilities of finding people alive," Vice-Admiral Alfeo Battelli told reporters in the southern Italian port of Brindisi. "Our ships will continue the search for the eventual recovery of bodies."

Some of the 34 survivors said more than 100 refugees may have been on the ancient Russian-made harbour patrol craft when it went down on Friday night after colliding with a navy ship trying to prevent it entering Italian waters.
They feared many had died and said those on board included children. Four bodies have been recovered so far.
The Italian news agency Ansa, in a report from Vlore, the Albanian port from where the boat left, quoted witnesses as saying that there were "no fewer than 120 people" on board.
"More than 50 of us died," one Albanian man shouted to reporters on the dock in Brindisi on Friday.
Italy's top navy official said that while he could not exclude that more than four people had died, he believed the boat was too small to have contained many people below deck.
"I can't believe that there were that many people on board ... it seems exaggerated to me that there could have been 100...," Admiral Angelo Mariani said in Rome.
"I cannot exclude unfortunately that there were other people on board but I don't think there could have been too many more below deck," Mariani said.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi said the navy operation to patrol the Adriatic and stem a tide of refugees would continue because it had Albanian government approval.
"This event shows that the international operation to help Albania has to begin as soon as possible," Prodi said.
The U.N. Security Council has authorised an international mission to help the country recover from violence and anarchy.
However Albania said later that the accident could have been avoided and asked Prodi to open an investigation.
The navy said it had opened an administrative enquiry while magistrates in Brindisi were also investigating the causes of the sinking.
Albanian parliamentary speaker Pjeter Arbnori slammed Italy's handling of the incident, saying "the boat should have been accompanied to Italy's coast instead of being blocked".
Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta sent a letter of condolences to Albanian counterpart Shaqir Vukaj, expressing his and the Italian armed forces' sadness at the tragedy.
The Italian navy said the Albanian boat was hit after it had cut across the bows of the corvette Sibilla.
"As far as we are concerned, it was they who hit us," Mariani said. "The accident happened because the Albanian ship behaved in an unpredictable and irresponsible way."
He said Tirana had told Italy that the Albanian boat was piloted by "local criminals".
Italy, concerned that many Albanian refugees are looking for a better life abroad rather than fleeing real danger, has ordered the navy to try to halt the flow.
The operation involves intercepting Albanian ships outside Italian waters and advising them to turn back.
More than 13,000 Albanians have reached Italy over the past two weeks on a flotilla of ancient boats after rebels in the south took control of towns in an armed insurrection.
